author: @FrankCurzio
text:
@BillAckman, I’m a little stoned. So hopefully this comes out ok… 

But you (and every person in the top 1%) will lose 25% of your wealth based on this thesis. 

At 3% inflation, the gap between the upper and lower class will widen dramatically. 

In other words, the 1% (who own assets that benefit from higher inflation) will get richer… 

While millions of people fall out of the middle class - and into a lower bucket of those having trouble making ends meet. 

That’s millions more Americans who will struggle with “affordability” - a huge topic that just provided a landslide win for the Democrats. 

If their costs keep going up (at close to 10% every 3 years based on the new Fed benchmark)… how do you think they’ll vote? 

Now we’re looking at a Democrat controlled government over a sustained period - since higher costs (3% annually) will continue pushing tons of red voters into blue voters. 

Once this happens, how much do you think your wealth tax will be? 5%? 10%? 

We’ll see more unions and the govt will enact collective bargaining rights for rideshare drivers. That suddenly changes your long position in Uber - to a short. 

Imagine being taxed on “unrealized gains?”

That’s a possibility in a Democrat controlled government (it was in Biden’s 2024 Billionaire Minimum Income Tax proposal). Would you continue to manage money knowing the risk/reward for your investors is no longer favorable if every one of your investments is taxed on unrealized gains? 

You’ll see new taxes on luxury homes… Every tax loophole will close… and forget offshore accounts since the Democrats said (publicly) they will punish any country that help billionaires avoid the US tax code. 

Probably better for the Fed to fight the good “2% inflation target” fight. 

Worst case… the Fed makes a mistake and tightens too much. The world economy goes into recession for 
12 months. Then the Fed eases aggressively. 

Markets roar back to new highs in 24-36 months. That’s been the playbook dating back to the 80s. 

I’d rather take the 2-3 year option - knowing the markets will go through some pain…than change a Fed mandate that could destroy my long-term wealth in a socialist America. 

Just my 10
cents. But what do I know?
quoted_text:
I think the Fed is about to make another mistake on December 9th. Financial conditions have tightened massively. For example, @SpaceX, an investment grade company, just raised secured debt financing at an 8.259% interest rate versus below 6% for its unsecured bond offering at the time of its IPO. 

The cost of equity capital has also increased materially with the recent substantial decline in the stock market. 

The Fed’s 2% inflation ambition is misguided. Geopolitical risk and the required investment in global military spending, de globalization and tariffs, and the massive AI infrastructure and related energy investment are features of the world that did not exist when the 2% target was set. 3% inflation is a more realistic ambition in the new world. 

The Fed will put the U.S. and world in recession if it continues to raise rates in a failed attempt to drive inflation to 2%. 

Tell me why I am wrong.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Gold just lost its fight with the Fed.

Gold is down about a third from its January record near $5,600. It fell below $3,700 this week right after Fed minutes showed broad support for more rate hikes.

Gold pays you nothing. Cash pays over 4%. While the Fed keeps hiking, that math wins every time.

And Iran heating up didn't save it (some safe haven).

The miners get it worse. Gold drops, costs keep rising... Agnico Eagle warned diesel alone could add up to $80 an ounce in 2027. Gold miner funds ($GDX) lost 23% in three months.

I was bullish on gold earlier this month. But back in May I said higher rates are terrible for something that pays no interest, and right now that argument is WINNING.

Yet $2.7B of new money still went into gold funds in October. The last holders haven't quit.

When they do, Agnico Eagle ($AEM) is the well-run miner I'd scale into slowly.

-

For anyone new here, I'm Frank. 30 years on Wall Street, and I post what's moving the market as it happens. Follow me @FrankCurzio for more.
